title: Verifier-integrated LLM intent-to-configuration pipeline: end-to-end safety and rollback evaluation
abstract: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired experiment (CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001) to test whether integrating an automated network verifier (and automated rollback) into an LLM intent→configuration pipeline reduces unsafe enactments in emulated NetOps tasks. Using a shared-initial-generation policy with gpt-5-mini across 150 paired intents (300 episodes), we ran two confirmatory pipelines per task: LLM-only (baseline) and LLM+verifier (guarded). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) accepted all generated configurations for both pipelines (150/150 valid per pipeline). Consequently the preregistered primary confirmatory comparison is untestable for the planned benefit (paired difference = 0.0 pp; exact McNemar p = 1.0) because no verifier-detected violations occurred. We therefore (1) present the full, artifact-grounded execution and scoring traces, (2) give a concise, evidence-backed summary of the validator acceptance predicates used in this run and point to representative artifact files and hashes, (3) diagnose likely reasons for the observed ceiling effect, and (4) provide reproducible recommendations and concrete next-step designs (harder, stateful, and adversarial task banks; multi-model and multi-verifier comparisons) to stress verifier-sensitive failure modes. All raw transcripts, validator traces, scoring JSONs, analysis scripts, and sha256 hashes are archived in the execution bundle referenced below.

sections.introduction: Intent-driven NetOps promises large productivity gains by mapping operator intent into low-level device configurations via LLMs. However, unsafe or out-of-order configurations can cause outages or security exposures, so verifier-and-rollback machinery is widely advocated to bound operational risk. We preregistered CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001 to test whether a verifier-block (plus optional automatic rollback) reduces unsafe enactments versus an LLM-only baseline under a paired design. Contributions: (i) a fully preregistered, deterministic paired experiment and archived evidence bundle; (ii) an artifact-grounded concise description of the deterministic validator acceptance predicates used in the run and representative evaluation files with sha256; (iii) confirmatory results showing a ceiling effect (no verifier-detected violations), diagnostic analysis with preserved raw traces, and prescriptive recommendations for future stress-testing benchmarks. The preregistration, execution manifest, and full artifact hashes are provided in the archive (preregistration SHA-256: 66fbf2c56649115c66412326fcc739ebacced84ec2df3fca796f4e7eac4a9b04).
sections.related_work: We position this work within three strands: (1) LLM-based intent-to-configuration and intent translation for NetOps (surveys and intent-translation studies, e.g., Nguyen et al., 2024, doi:10.1002/nem.2313; OpenAlex records W7114889968, W7155247165, W7161354925); (2) generate–validate–repair and verifier-augmented generation for code/configuration safety (RAG, test-in-the-loop APR, and verifier-assisted pipelines); and (3) network-change verification and digital-twin approaches for pre-deployment validation (Batfish/NetKAT/HS-based families). All cited bibliography items appearing in the manuscript were verified against the archived literature record list supplied with the run and are included in the referenced record list.
sections.methodology: Preregistration (CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001) and design: paired confirmatory experiment, planned confirmatory tasks = 150, stratified by intent ambiguity (benign / ambiguous / partially-specified). Model and generation policy: single shared-initial candidate per task produced by gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); generation budget limited to one initial call per task (maximum repair calls per task = 1). Pipelines: (A) baseline LLM-only (enact candidate as-is); (B) guarded LLM+verifier-block (validator inspects candidate; block if violation); rollback path (preregistered) would be invoked only on verifier-detected violations. Validator and harness: the run used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the verifier/validator implementation; full model_configuration and execution artifacts are archived under execution/model_configuration.json (sha256: 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa) and execution/execution_manifest.json (artifact manifest path recorded in the bundle). Primary estimand and test: per-task unsafe-enactment rate difference (baseline minus guarded), analyzed with paired exact McNemar two-sided test (Bonferroni-adjusted per preregistration). Missingness, contamination, retry, and exclusion rules were enforced exactly as preregistered.
sections.results: Execution summary (artifact-backed): run start 2026-08-25T18:55:00Z; complete 2026-08-25T19:10:50Z (execution_manifest and analysis artifacts archived). Episodes executed: 300 (150 paired tasks). Model calls used: 150 (shared-initial per task). No failed episodes, no infrastructure-missing episodes, and no preregistered exclusions. Scoring and confirmatory outcomes (artifact-backed): baseline valid-configurations = 150/150 (100.0%); guarded valid-configurations = 150/150 (100.0%); paired contingency n11=150, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. Paired estimate (guarded minus baseline) = 0.0 percentage points; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap resamples=10000, seed=1729). Because the verifier detected zero violations in the confirmatory set, the preregistered secondary estimands (rollback-success proportion, median time-to-rollback) are not applicable for inferential testing and therefore untested; raw traces showing absence of rollback events are archived (representative scoring JSONs: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json sha256=974cab2a4237a0fca9ebe61616d6b471cf2e6bfbd5e5cbabe82701957cbeea14; execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json sha256=9ae4c9db62d09a44b547cc57e191582c1e303ab95a91fe5c44085fa5cdbd0701). Contamination detectors flagged zero contaminated tasks (analysis/contamination_summary.csv sha256=389227f0d1e81239c7498abd4944a04c59c92c5fa042b990e332796cd61c3222). Full raw transcripts, validator traces, and scoring files are archived per the execution manifest.
sections.discussion: Interpretation and diagnostic analysis: the confirmatory run produced a ceiling outcome: both pipelines yielded validator-acceptable configurations for all confirmatory tasks, preventing demonstration of the preregistered verifier benefit in this experimental regime. From the archived validator traces the following, artifact-backed observations are relevant: (1) the validator records include per-episode fields 'required_command_count', 'parsed_command_count', 'violation_count', 'violation_codes', and 'valid' (see execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json sha256=974cab2a... for a representative example), and all confirmatory episodes show violation_count==0 and valid==true; (2) the synthetic intent bank (CNSM-AI-NetOps-Intent-Bench-v1) produced configurations that met the validator's required_command_count and dependency checks as encoded in the validator traces; (3) no verifier-block or rollback events were triggered in the confirmatory set, so H2 and rollback metrics are untestable. Validator-choice justification and consequence: the preregistration discussed Batfish-style open-source verifiers as conceptual references but allowed a verifier interface at execution time. The executed run used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (recorded in the scoring JSONs and model_configuration.json sha256=1acce925...), which enforces the acceptance predicates found in the archived traces (see next subsection). Because different verifiers operationalize invariants differently, validator selection plausibly contributed to the ceiling effect; this reduces external validity across verifier families and motivates future multi-verifier comparisons. Recommendations for future studies (artifact-grounded): (i) construct adversarial/stateful task banks that target dependency/temporal invariants (examples and patterns can be derived from the 'difficulty' fields in the archived validator traces); (ii) run multi-model and multi-verifier permutations to expose verifier-sensitive failure modes; (iii) include live-state or transient invariants (timed sequences) rather than purely syntactic requirements; (iv) preserve the preregistered paired design and robust contamination detectors while intentionally injecting verifier-challenging examples.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and ran a deterministic paired study to test whether adding a verifier and automated rollback reduces unsafe LLM-generated NetOps enactments. In the chosen emulated task bank with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, no verifier-detected violations occurred across 150 confirmatory pairs; thus the preregistered primary hypothesis could not be demonstrated (paired difference = 0.0 pp; exact McNemar p = 1.0). The principal scientific value of this run is not a policy conclusion about verifiers, but a detailed, fully archived empirical lesson: (i) benchmarks and validators must be jointly designed to expose verifier-conditional failure modes; (ii) single-model, single-validator, and synthetic-task regimes can produce ceiling effects that prevent meaningful confirmatory inference; and (iii) our artifact bundle (preregistration, raw transcripts, scoring JSONs, validator traces, and analysis scripts with sha256 hashes) is available to the community to enable targeted follow-up studies with adversarial and stateful scenarios. We release the full run artifacts and provide concrete guidance for next-step evaluation designs that are more likely to stress verifier boundaries and reveal operational gains from verifiers and rollback machinery.

disclosure_statement: Human and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the broad topic family and supplied the initial master prompt and autonomy constraints before the autonomy lock. Pre-lock: collaborative development produced reusable harness components and rehearsal scripts; pre-lock experimental results were not used as confirmatory evidence. Post-lock autonomy: after the lock the AI autonomously performed literature review, research-question selection, machine-readable preregistration (CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001, preregistration SHA-256=66fbf2c56649115c66412326fcc739ebacced84ec2df3fca796f4e7eac4a9b04), deterministic experiment implementation, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, automated peer-review checks, and finalization. Models and orchestration: experiments used a single hosted model recorded as gpt-5-mini (provider: openai_responses in the execution manifest). Adapter/orchestration family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Prompts and generation semantics: the run used a shared_initial_candidate policy (one initial generation call per task; at most one repair call per task) as frozen in the preregistration; exact frozen prompt text and adapter instructions are archived in the execution bundle (see execution/model_configuration.json sha256=1acce92558ed...). Verifier and validator: the executed validator is recorded as deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and its per-episode traces and acceptance outputs are archived in execution/scoring/*.json (representative files: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json sha256=974cab2a4237a0fca9ebe6...). The preregistration discussed Batfish-style open-source verifiers as conceptual lead examples; the actual run used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (artifact-backed). Preregistered procedures: sampling plan (150 confirmatory tasks), exclusion and contamination detectors (auto-exclude non-RFC1918 public IPs; exact-match fingerprinting), retry policy, stopping rules (>2% contamination abort), and statistical analysis (paired McNemar with Bonferroni adjustment) were all recorded and enforced. Execution artifacts and reproducibility: the run produced 300 episodes (150 paired tasks), used 150 model calls, and completed with no failed episodes. All raw outputs, model-call traces, scoring JSONs, validator traces, analysis scripts, and sha256 hashes are archived and referenced in execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis artifacts (see analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv sha256=c2ba9cdb...). Human editing: no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock; all manuscript revisions requested by reviewers were implemented autonomously using the archived artifacts. Deviations and restarts: none beyond automated retries described in the preregistration. Limitations: the study used synthetic, emulated tasks and a single model and validator; archived contamination detectors are heuristic and cannot guarantee absence of subtle training-data leakage. Contact: the execution bundle (preregistration, raw logs, scoring JSONs, analysis scripts, and full hash manifest) is archived under the execution manifest listed in the artifact bundle (execution/execution_manifest.json).
limitations: Ceiling effect in confirmatory run: both pipelines produced validator-acceptable configurations in all 150 confirmatory tasks, making the preregistered primary and secondary inferential comparisons untestable in this regime.
Synthetic/emulated benchmark: CNSM-AI-NetOps-Intent-Bench-v1 is synthetic and may not exercise live-state, timing, or adversarial invariants present in production NetOps.

Single-model and single-validator scope: experiments used only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; results do not generalize across LLM families or verifier implementations (e.g., Batfish-style tools).

Validator specificity and acceptance predicates: the validator used here enforces the acceptance predicates visible in the archived validator traces (e.g., required_command_count, parsed_command_count, violation_count==0). Those predicates differ across verifier families and likely influenced the ceiling effect; full validator configuration is archived (execution/model_configuration.json sha256=1acce925...).

Construct validity: the chosen validator-detected 'unsafe enactment' metric is an imperfect proxy for operational harms such as transient reachability loss, timing-dependent outages, or side effects not encoded in the validator rules.
Contamination detection limits: deterministic detectors flagged zero contaminated tasks, but heuristic scans cannot eliminate the possibility of subtle training-data leakage.
